name: A Least Cornerless Ample Family Has a Maximum Core of Order at Most 99
statement: Let $H$ have minimum cardinality among all nonempty cornerless ample families, and suppose $|H|<299$. Then either $H$ is a pseudogeometric maximum class, or its antipodal-double maximum core is obtained from opposite conditionings on a set $R$ of size $r\ge2$ and satisfies $(r+1)|A|+1\le|H|$ and $|A|\le\lfloor297/(r+1)\rfloor\le99$.
proof: Assume the conditioning set is nonempty. Equality in the general bound would give $H=A\times P$. If $A$ were cornerless it would be a smaller nonempty cornerless ample family; if it had a corner, pairing that corner with an endpoint of $P$ would give a corner of $H$. Both contradict the choice of $H$, so the bound is strict. When $r=1$, the only antipodal path is the whole one-cube and equality is automatic, hence $r\ge2$. Finally $|H|\le298$ gives $(r+1)|A|\le297$ and therefore $|A|\le99$.
comments: This strengthens the general sub-Hall core bound by using cardinality minimality to exclude the equality product case and the one-coordinate case.
